title: tebako-bench suite v1
description: The benchmark suite document (spec 27 §2): workloads + targets + run_policy. This schema is the STRUCTURAL contract; the tebako-bench crate's serde model is the same shape (kept MECE by the unit-test cross-check). Semantic rules beyond shape — {doc} arity, git ref pinning to a 40-hex commit (pattern-checked here), registries being spec-04 references — are the model's/run engine's. Unknown keys are tolerated at every level for forward compatibility; schema_version pins the version.

baseline.description: The arm the report's speedup column is computed against: an exact target id, or a prefix resolving to exactly one target per workload (e.g. "on-system" in the runtime suite). Absent = the v1-prefix law.

workloads.description: The documents to compile, or (runtime suite) the interpreter invocations. Order is not semantic; ids are unique (checked semantically).

targets.description: The arms under test (spec 27 §1, §10.1). A full suite declares one target of each kind unless an arm is genuinely meaningless.

id.description: DNS-label-ish identifier, used as a key in result records.

opt_in.description: When true the workload runs only on explicit opt-in (e.g. needs credentials — the OIML r060 private-fonts case). A skipped opt-in workload emits NO result rows.

source.description: Optional (2026-09-17 amendment): interpreter workloads (the runtime suite) have no document; {doc} in argv is then a semantic error.

argv.description: The argument vector passed to the target's entrypoint. Substitutions: '{doc}' (the workload document's path in the run scratch; requires source), '{fixture}' (the ioread data file, resolved per target — in-image for runtime-exe arms, host path otherwise), '{classes}' (the in-leg compiled Java classes directory). Every other token is literal.

timeout_s.description: Per-run timeout in seconds. Expiry kills the child tree and records status "timeout" — a benchmark may be slow, never hung.

path.description: vendored: file path relative to the repo root. git: the document's path inside the pinned tree.

ref.description: The pinned 40-hex commit. Floating refs (branches, tags) are invalid: reproducibility is the point of the pin. Fetched as the host's in-process HTTPS archive — never a git shell-out.

exit.description: Expected process exit status (the spec 26 §1 expect rule).

files.description: Scratch-relative output paths that must exist and be non-empty after the run. May be EMPTY (2026-09-17 amendment): interpreter workloads assert on the exit status alone.

kind.description: v1-exe: the packed-mn release asset (asset from platforms.yaml). v2-managed: registry install + shim dispatch, warm store. v2-press: fat tpkg assembled in-leg from verified published artifacts. on-system: the host toolchain binary (CI-provisioned, version-pinned). runtime-exe: the tebako runtime pair fetched sha256-verified from its factory release.

payload.description: name@version — the registry payload reference (v2 kinds).

registries.description: spec 04 registry references the v2 arms resolve the payload through.

fat.description: v2-press: carry the runtime as a slot (the one-file contract). v2 packages are fat in this harness by definition; the flag exists for the suite author's explicitness.

program.description: on-system: the host toolchain binary, PATH-resolved (the workflow provisions it).

version_probe.description: on-system: the argv that prints the toolchain's version; the parity probe runs the tebako arm with the same argv.

version_expect.description: on-system: the version token BOTH arms' probe output must contain (the fair-comparison invariant; a mismatch is a named skip, never a skewed comparison).

lang_version.description: The interpreter version the pair carries (the asset names embed it).

runtime.description: runtime-exe: the factory release the tebako runtime pair is fetched from, sha256-verified against the release's per-asset sidecars.

compile_classes.description: on-system java: the vendored .java directory (repo-relative) compiled ONCE in-leg with the on-system javac; both JVMs run the same .class files.

warmup.description: Unmeasured runs per (workload × target) priming the fontist/relaton/OS caches before measurement.

repetitions.description: Measured warm runs per (workload × target). The statistics live or die on this N.

cold_repetitions.description: Measured cold runs — each preceded by the spec 27 §5 cache wipe; reported separately as install/first-boot metrics, never mixed into warm statistics.

interleave.description: true: rotate targets A/B/C per iteration to decorrelate runner drift. false: each target to completion in turn (debugging only).
